card.name: Baba Karam
card.tagline: Playful Persian character dance mimicking the urban tough-guy
card.profile: Baba Karam is a Persian urban social/character dance performed to the song 'Baba Karam,' which dates to the Qajar dynasty (1794-1925) and was first sung by Hossein Hamedanian around 1920, later revived by Vigen Derderian; it belongs to the koocheh-bazaari / roo-hozi genre (middleeasterndancing.com). The dance portrays the jahel or luti - undereducated urban 'tough guys' living by a code of honor - using a fedora and neckerchief, posturing strut, hip sways, hand movements and expressive eyebrow and lip play (middleeasterndancing.com). Wikipedia notes Baba Karam is sometimes used as a term for contemporary Persian hip-hop dancing (Iranian dance, Wikipedia).
card.insight: It was popularized by the 'tough guy' film genre and by dancer Jamileh; whether it evolved from real jahel dancing or as a caricature remains unconfirmed (middleeasterndancing.com).
card.image_significance: Swagger of the Tehran tough-guy. A representative image shows a line or row formation, often with canes, swords or flowing veils — Tehran, Iran.
